explainBack.question: Why did adding 20,167 private protein structures make the model score better on the held-out test, and why doesn't that better score mean a medicine is coming?
explainBack.answer: The private structures gave the model many more real examples of how proteins and drug-like molecules fit together than public data alone contains, so its predictions on unseen test structures improved. But that score only measures prediction accuracy on one test set. A medicine requires further separate steps the report does not include: releasing or validating the model, peer review, making and lab-testing candidate molecules, and clinical trials showing patients actually benefit.
explainBack.expectedEvidence: An accurate answer must cite the private-data fine-tuning and held-out evaluation from P002–P003 and the benchmark/clinical-trial distinction from P004, retaining the not-public and not-peer-reviewed limits.
explainBack.assessment: The article fully supports this answer: P002 supplies the data-to-model event, P003 supplies the held-out mechanism and the two limits, and P004 supplies the missing downstream stages. Explain-back passes.

unseenTransfer.scenario: An insurance company announces that its fraud-detection AI, fine-tuned on a rival consortium's pooled private claims data, flagged 30% more fraudulent claims correctly on an internal held-out test set, and a headline says 'AI will slash your insurance premiums.'
unseenTransfer.question: Using this article's mechanism, what does the announcement actually establish, and what would need to be reported before believing the premium claim?
unseenTransfer.answer: It establishes only a benchmark result: more private training examples improved prediction accuracy on one internal test set. Like the protein model, that is a model comparison, not an outcome for people. Before believing the premium claim, a reader should look for the later stages: independent or external validation of the test, deployment in real claims handling, and evidence that measured savings were actually passed to customers as lower premiums.
unseenTransfer.expectedEvidence: The transfer must reuse the private-data-improves-held-out-score mechanism (P002–P003) and the benchmark-versus-real-world-outcome ladder and next-question habit (P004).
unseenTransfer.assessment: The article's mechanism resolves this unseen case without extra concepts — the reader can classify the announcement and name the missing evidence stages. Transfer passes.
